text:
kai: dropping a design note — thinking about an 'adaptive-slot' approach where we decouple small-request queues from bulk coalescing pools. goal: keep p99 for short chats while not blowing up throughput. sketch attached.

maria: do you mean physically separate queues or logical lanes on same queue?

kai: physical-ish. separate lightweight lane for <32 tokens requests that bypass long-window coalescer. lane gets fast-turnaround slots and a tiny per-tenant credit.

tj: concern: splitting queues can starve the larger batches and hurt GPU utilization. how do we avoid oscillation? :thinking:

kai: plan is: probabilistic admission for medium requests, and a circuit that temporarily routes extra small requests into bulk path when utilization drops below threshold. think hysteresis + dampening.

anya: how does this interact with KV cache warming? small lane will generate more cache misses if requests are shorter/prefix-sketch-y.

lee: we measured earlier that tiny requests are ~40% of bursts but only ~10% of tokens. if we prioritize them we cut p99 by ~60ms but throughput drops 5%.

maria: 5% throughput loss might be acceptable if it saves SLAs. need numbers across tail, not just avg.

ops-bot: deploy-check: make sure new queue flags are gated behind feature-flag "adaptive_slot_v1".

kai: agreed. rough config prototype: 
```
queues:
  small_lane:
    max_inflight: 64
    slot_ttl_ms: 50
    tenant_credit: 2
  coalesce_pool:
    window_ms: 8
    max_batch_tokens: 4096
routing:
  admission_policy: \"probabilistic\"
  util_threshold_pct: 72
```

lee: add telemetry hooks: per-lane enqueue_rate, headroom, kv_miss_rate, and an impact signal for model latency regression.

anya: we should also consider soft-fallback: if slot acquisition fails, instead of retrying, attach request to best-effort small-queue that accepts degraded QoS. reduces enqueue churn.

tj: eviction policy question: when small_lane is saturated and a burst of medium arrives, do we preempt small slots? that could hurt p99 again.

kai: no preemption by default. we prefer adaptive throttling upstream (client hints) and a temporary probabilistic backoff for small requests when GPU core utilization is high. preemption only as last resort and logged.

maria: rollout plan? canary on 10% of hosts with synthetic microbench (mixed small/medium traces). compare 99/995 percentiles and token throughput.

lee: also monitor downstream cost metrics — batch efficiency, idle_gpu_ms. if cost per token rises >3% we roll back.

anya: note for docs: expose tenant_credit as tuning knob but warn users about bursty clients.

kai: next steps: I'll spin up a prototype in the staging runner, wire telemetry, and open an RFC-style PR with experiments/plots. tagging @maria @tj for review before canary. :thumbsup:

maria: SGTM. add test that simulates KV-warmup penalty.

tj: will review, ping me when PR is up.

ops-bot: reminder: create incident runbook entry for 'adaptive_slot_v1' fallback sequence.
